newsitem.title: UK: FSU oil export jump means demand fell in '96 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: FSU oil export jump means demand fell in '96 - IEA.

text.p: The countries of the Former Soviet Union (FSU) exported 360,000 barrels per day (bpd) more oil in December 1996 than a year earlier, said the International Energy Agency (IEA) On Tuesday.

This big year-on-year jump in exports which has lifted the figure for the whole of the fourth quarter of 1996, caused the IEA to revise downwards its figure for "apparent" demand which is calculated by taking the difference between oil production and exports.

The estimate of FSU apparent demand in the fourth quarter 1996 was adjusted downwards by 500,000 bpd to 4.3 million bpd which is 600,000 bpd lower than year earlier figures, the IEA said in it's December Monthly Oil Market Report.
The latest demand estimate is consistent with evidence of lower-than-expected economic activity, higher oil product prices, a slow down in the growth of car use and milder weather.
Despite small rises in demand in the first three quarters of 1996, demand for the whole year is now estimated to have fallen by 400,000 bpd to 4.3 million bpd, the IEA said.
This represents a year on year drop of 8.5 percent but the IEA expects that to slow to a drop of 0.2 percent this year.
Net oil exports have been higher than anticipated, partly as a threat to ban or heavily tax exports has not been carried out, leading to a downard revision to apparent demand, the report said.
